title: improv·artist · fluid (Helen Frankenthaler)
mutation_directive: improv artist: fluid via Helen Frankenthaler

improv_extras.practice: soak-stain; thinned pigment soaks the canvas; geological flow

v1.feedback: The soak-stain concept lands: orthographic camera, diluted Frankenthaler palette, and pooling/gravity logic all show the linked idea drove the design rather than being bolted on. The main weakness is that 80k particles at alpha 0.6 with 2–3.5px point size produce soft diffuse washes that read more as translucent blobs than distinct stain edges — Frankenthaler's pours have sharp wet-boundary rings where pigment concentrates at the meniscus. Add a rim-darkening term that boosts alpha near the convex hull of each pool (approximate via distance-from-centroid thresholding) to get that characteristic stain-edge halo. The gentle breathing oscillation is nice but nearly invisible — consider letting the flow field evolve more over time so the pour feels like it's still soaking rather than settling into a static arrangement after the initial animation.

v2.feedback: The soak-stain concept lands well — pools expand with rim-darkening meniscus concentration, the palette is genuinely Frankenthaler (raw sienna, cerulean wash, dusty rose), and the orthographic 2D framing is correct for this painterly idiom. Two things to push: the flow displacement is uniform sinusoidal swirl, which reads more like a screensaver than geological pigment seepage — replace the analytical flowField with a slower, heterogeneous warp that lets pools bleed into each other asymmetrically, the way thinned acrylic actually wicks along canvas grain. Second, the particle alpha is low enough to feel washy but the pools remain too circular even after flow — add elongation along a per-pool random axis so the stains read as poured rather than stamped.
